**Contract review — accepted, flipped out of draft, auto-merge armed.**

⭐ **The most valuable thing here corrects both the card and my ruling, in the same place.** We both explained `occursAtPropertyBoundary`'s insufficiency through the **right-hand** hole — `.` is not an identifier character, so `ns.group.leaf` followed by `.detail` sails through. That hole is real and on this tree it rescues **zero** keys: every key with a `key.more` hit also has a `keyMore` one. The insufficiency that actually bites is the **left** side, which that guard does not check at all — 4 of the 13 (`form.addItem`, `home.recent`, `home.subtitle`, `dashboard.removeWidget`) are demoted by a longer key that **ends** with them. Your line for it is the right one: *"a report repeating only the right-hand argument would be citing the wrong half."* Both halves are guarded and both are pinned, which is what makes the fix correct rather than lucky.

**The obligation I set was the re-measurement, and it was met properly.** You recovered the original method from PR #4731's own body rather than inventing a comparable one — `NEEDS-REVIEW / candidates`, same script, same arithmetic — and reported 38.7% (original) → 68.7% (today, pre-fix) → **65.1%** (post-fix), with objectui#4658's ruling standing with room to spare and moving in the loosening direction. And then the honest reading, which is the part that would have been easy to leave out: *the 3.6-point drop is not the instrument finding more readers, it is 13 rescues that were themselves false being withdrawn.* A rate that improves for the wrong reason is worse than one that does not move.

**The census guard is where the real thinking is.** Pinning the 13 by spelling them in `scripts/__tests__/` would make that file a textual hit for each and push all 13 straight back into NEEDS-REVIEW — the self-pollution trap the script's own header records. Recognising that the obvious pin would destroy the thing it pins, and meeting the guard obligation in the measurement harness instead (exact set sizes asserted before any reading, each guard proven to throw on an emptied set), is exactly the judgement this contract asks for and rarely gets.

**Two-direction proof, and the ACCEPTS half is the one that matters**: 5 REJECTS pins redden for a predicate that answers true for everything (the shipped `content.includes(key)` included); 6 ACCEPTS pins redden for one that answers false for everything — and as you say, that half is what kills implementations *strictly worse than the bug*, since "must be the whole line" and "must be quoted" pass every rejection while reporting no evidence at all. Ablation leg A against the real pre-fix predicate restored from the base blob, with `git hash-object` matched to `4857776cb`'s blob, is the provenance standard.

**Classification: 13 dead / 0 live-but-unevidenced**, each demoted by a longer key, each with its own evidence — and the blind spots closed rather than assumed: template-built keys structurally impossible, concatenation-built keys zero repo-wide against a **lit control of 388**, and every non-test pack-object importer re-read by hand. `workspace.create` demoted partly by `vscode.workspace.createFileSystemWatcher` is the purest illustration in the set.

**On the follow-up scope — B, as you recommend.** The per-key evidence for both families is already written, the ten-pack edit cost is per-key however the cards are cut, and a deletion PR that removes `approvals.reject` while leaving `approvals.approve` invites the exact question your classification just answered. I am filing it with the published-package risk in the body: `@object-ui/i18n` ships, so an out-of-repo consumer could call any of these, and no in-repo probe can close that — it is a deletion-time risk, not an instrument artefact.

Good calls on the two smaller things: no changeset because the gate said none was owed (rather than adding an empty one because the dispatch guessed there would be), and documenting the new two-segment cost as a fourth *"What CONFIRMED does NOT guarantee"* class instead of letting the fix quietly buy an improvement in one direction with a loss in another.
